syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Identify whether a collection of objects is well defined and hence forms a set.
Write a set in roster form and in set-builder form and convert between the two.

topics.title: Empty, finite, infinite and equal sets

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise the empty set and distinguish it from sets such as {0}.
Classify a given set as finite or infinite.
Decide whether two sets are equal by comparing their elements.
Use the subset relation correctly and distinguish it from membership of an element.
Express subsets of R as open, closed and half-open intervals and in set-builder form.
Choose a suitable universal set for a given collection of sets.
Represent the universal set and its subsets with Venn diagrams.
Find the union and intersection of sets and use their basic properties.
Find the difference of two sets and identify disjoint sets.
Find the complement of a set with respect to a universal set and apply the complement laws.
Apply De Morgan's laws to complements of unions and intersections.
Use the equality of ordered pairs to find unknown values.
Form the cartesian product of two sets and recognise that A × B and B × A differ.
Find the number of elements in A × B using n(A × B) = n(A) n(B).
Define a relation from A to B as a subset of A × B.
Find the domain, codomain and range of a relation.
Count the relations from A to B as 2 raised to n(A) n(B).
Decide whether a relation is a function using the one-and-only-one-image rule.
Find the image of an element and the preimage of a value under a function.
Identify a linear function f(x) = mx + c from given ordered pairs.
Recognise identity, constant, polynomial and rational functions and their graphs.
Evaluate and describe the modulus, signum and greatest integer functions.
Find the domain and range of simple real functions.
Find the sum, difference and product of two real functions.
Find the quotient of two real functions and state where it is defined.
Convert angles between degree and radian measure using pi radians = 180 degrees.
Use l = r theta to relate arc length, radius and the angle in radians.

topics.title: Trigonometric functions on the unit circle

concepts.learning_objective: Define sin x and cos x as coordinates of a point on the unit circle and find their zeros.
Use sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 and related identities to find the other functions from one value.
Determine the sign of each trigonometric function in the four quadrants.
State domains and ranges of trigonometric functions and use their periodicity to evaluate values.

topics.title: Sum and difference of two angles

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the formulas for sin, cos and tan of (x + y) and (x - y).
Simplify trigonometric functions of allied angles such as pi/2 + x and pi - x.
Use the double- and triple-angle formulas for sin, cos and tan.
Convert sums of sines and cosines into products and simplify expressions.

topics.title: The need for complex numbers and their definition

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why i = sqrt(-1) is introduced and identify the real and imaginary parts of a complex number.
Use the equality of complex numbers to find unknown real values by equating real and imaginary parts.

topics.title: Addition, subtraction and multiplication of complex numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Add and subtract complex numbers and identify the additive identity and additive inverse.
Multiply complex numbers using (a + ib)(c + id) = (ac − bd) + i(ad + bc) and its properties.

topics.title: Division of complex numbers and powers of i

concepts.learning_objective: Divide one complex number by another by multiplying by the multiplicative inverse (or the conjugate of the denominator).
Evaluate integral powers of i using i^(4k) = 1, i^(4k+1) = i, i^(4k+2) = −1 and i^(4k+3) = −i.

topics.title: Square roots of negative real numbers and identities

concepts.learning_objective: Find the square roots of a negative real number and recognise that sqrt(a) × sqrt(b) = sqrt(ab) fails when a and b are both negative.
Apply algebraic identities such as (z₁ + z₂)³ and z₁² − z₂² = (z₁ + z₂)(z₁ − z₂) to complex numbers.

topics.title: Modulus and conjugate of a complex number

concepts.learning_objective: Find the modulus |z| = sqrt(a² + b²) and use |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| and |z₁/z₂| = |z₁|/|z₂|.
Find the conjugate of a complex number and use z·z̄ = |z|².
Find the multiplicative inverse of a non-zero complex number as z̄/|z|².

topics.title: Argand plane and representation of complex numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Represent a complex number x + iy as the point (x, y) in the Argand plane and interpret its modulus as distance from the origin.
Interpret the conjugate of a complex number as the mirror image of its point in the real axis.
Recognise an inequality and model a simple situation by one.
Distinguish strict inequalities (<, >) from slack inequalities (<=, >=).
Identify linear inequalities in one and two variables and tell them apart from non-linear ones.
State the rules for adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing both sides of an inequality.
Apply the reversal of the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

topics.title: Solution sets in N, Z and R; interval notation

concepts.learning_objective: Find the solution set of a linear inequality when the variable is natural, integer or real.
Write the real solutions of an inequality in interval notation.

topics.title: Graphical representation on the number line

concepts.learning_objective: Represent x < a, x > a, x <= a and x >= a correctly on a number line.
Solve a linear inequality and choose the correct number-line graph of its solutions.
Form and solve inequalities for minimum marks needed to reach an average.
Find pairs of consecutive odd or even integers satisfying given conditions.
Form and solve inequalities for lengths and perimeters.

topics.title: Double inequalities and systems of inequalities

concepts.learning_objective: Solve double inequalities by operating on all three parts together.
Solve a system of linear inequalities in one variable as the common part of the solutions.
Convert a temperature range between Celsius and Fahrenheit using a double inequality.
Form and solve inequalities for the concentration of a mixture of solutions.
Find the range of a quantity from a formula and a given range of another quantity.
Apply the fundamental principle of counting to events occurring in succession.
Count arrangements when repetition is or is not allowed and when positions carry conditions.

topics.title: Permutations of Distinct Objects and Factorial Notation

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate and simplify expressions written in factorial notation.
Count arrangements of distinct objects, including when some objects must stay together.
Use the formula nPr = n!/(n - r)! to evaluate permutations and solve equations in n.
Distinguish counts with and without repetition of objects.

topics.title: Permutations when Objects are not Distinct

concepts.learning_objective: State the number of permutations of n objects when some of them are alike.
Count arrangements of the letters of a word with repeated letters, with or without conditions.
Relate nCr to nPr and evaluate combinations.
Use the property nCr = nC(n - r) to solve problems.
Count selections of committees and groups under given conditions.

topics.title: Pascal's triangle and patterns in binomial expansions

concepts.learning_objective: Construct rows of Pascal's triangle and use them as coefficients of a binomial expansion.
Describe the patterns in the number of terms and the powers of a and b in the expansion of (a + b)^n.

topics.title: Binomial theorem for any positive integer n

concepts.learning_objective: State the binomial theorem and use it to find a specified term or coefficient of an expansion.
Identify binomial coefficients and the number of terms in the expansion of (a + b)^n.
Explain the steps of the proof of the binomial theorem by mathematical induction.

topics.title: Special cases of the binomial theorem

concepts.learning_objective: Expand (x - y)^n and determine the signs of its terms.
Use the expansion of (1 + x)^n with suitable values of x to evaluate sums of binomial coefficients.
Evaluate powers of numbers like 98 or 102 by writing them as a sum or difference of convenient numbers.
Compare large powers with given numbers using the first few terms of a binomial expansion.
Approximate powers such as (0.99)^5 using the first few terms of an expansion.

topics.title: Divisibility and identities using the binomial theorem

concepts.learning_objective: Prove divisibility and remainder results by expanding a suitable binomial.
Simplify sums and differences such as (a + b)^n + (a - b)^n and evaluate surd expressions with them.

topics.title: Sequences: terms, general term and recurrence

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish finite and infinite sequences and identify a sequence as a function on natural numbers.
Find terms of a sequence from a formula for its nth term.
Generate terms of a sequence such as the Fibonacci sequence from a recurrence relation.
Form the series associated with a sequence and find its sum.
Write and evaluate finite sums using sigma notation.

topics.title: Geometric progression and its general term

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise a G.P. and find its common ratio.
Use a_n = ar^(n-1) to find a term, the position of a term, or the G.P. itself.

topics.title: Sum to n terms of a G.P.

concepts.learning_objective: Apply S_n = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1) for r not equal to 1 and S_n = na for r = 1.
Solve real-life and special-series problems using the sum of a G.P.
Find the geometric mean of two positive numbers as the square root of their product.
Insert a given number of geometric means between two positive numbers.
Prove and apply A >= G for two positive numbers.
Find two positive numbers when their A.M. and G.M. are given.

topics.title: Recall: distance, section formula and area of a triangle

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the distance, section and mid-point formulae to points in the coordinate plane.
Use the area of a triangle in coordinates to find areas and test collinearity.
Relate the inclination of a line to its slope m = tan(theta).
Find the slope of a line through two given points.
Use slopes to decide whether two lines are parallel or perpendicular.
Test three points for collinearity using slopes.
Find the angle between two lines from their slopes using tan(theta) = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1m2)|.

topics.title: Horizontal, vertical, point-slope and two-point forms

concepts.learning_objective: Write equations of lines parallel to the coordinate axes.
Write the equation of a line through a point with a given slope.
Write the equation of a line through two given points.
Express a line as y = mx + c and read its slope and y-intercept.
Use x/a + y/b = 1 to write and interpret lines from their intercepts.
Convert the general equation Ax + By + C = 0 into other forms.

topics.title: Distance of a point from a line and between parallel lines

concepts.learning_objective: Find the perpendicular distance of a point from a line.
Find the distance between two parallel lines.

topics.title: Sections of a cone and degenerate conics

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the conic section formed from the angle beta between the cutting plane and the axis of a cone of semi-vertical angle alpha.
Identify the degenerate sections obtained when the plane passes through the vertex of the cone.
Write the equation of a circle from its centre and radius, or from given conditions.
Find the centre and radius of a circle from its general second-degree equation.
Find the focus, directrix and equation of a parabola in one of its four standard forms.
Find the length of the latus rectum of a parabola.
Define an ellipse and use the relation c^2 = a^2 - b^2 between its semi-axes and focal distance.
Compute and interpret the eccentricity e = c/a of an ellipse.

topics.title: Ellipse: standard equations and latus rectum

concepts.learning_objective: Find foci, vertices and the standard equation of an ellipse from given data.
Use the length 2b^2/a of the latus rectum of an ellipse.
Define a hyperbola and use c^2 = a^2 + b^2 and e = c/a.
Find foci, latus rectum and the standard equation of a hyperbola from given data.

topics.title: Coordinate axes, coordinate planes and octants

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three mutually perpendicular coordinate axes and the coordinate planes they determine.
Determine the octant of a point from the signs of its coordinates.

topics.title: Coordinates of a point in space

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the coordinates of a point as its signed perpendicular distances from the YZ, ZX and XY-planes.
State the form of the coordinates of points lying on the coordinate axes and coordinate planes.
Apply the distance formula to find the distance between two points in space.
Find the distance of a point from the origin.
Use distances to test collinearity and to classify triangles and quadrilaterals in space.
Form the equation of a set of points satisfying a distance condition.
Find the centroid of a triangle, or a missing vertex from the centroid.
Compute the average velocity of a moving body over a time interval from its distance-time relation.
Explain instantaneous velocity as the limiting value of average velocities over shrinking intervals.

topics.title: Limits: left hand and right hand limits

concepts.learning_objective: Find the left hand and right hand limits of a function at a point.
Decide whether the limit of a function exists at a point by comparing one-sided limits.

topics.title: Algebra of limits; limits of polynomials and rational functions

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the sum, product and quotient rules for limits with their conditions.
Evaluate limits of polynomial and rational functions, including 0/0 forms by factorisation.
Use the result that the limit of (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) as x tends to a is n a^(n-1).
State and apply the Sandwich Theorem for limits.
Evaluate limits using lim sin x/x = 1 and lim (1 - cos x)/x = 0 as x tends to 0.
Define the derivative at a point as a limit and interpret it as the slope of the tangent.
Find derivatives of simple functions from the first principle.

topics.title: Algebra of derivatives; derivatives of polynomials and trigonometric functions

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the sum, product (Leibnitz) and quotient rules of differentiation.
Differentiate polynomials and sin x, cos x using standard results.
Identify the measures of dispersion and why central tendency alone does not describe data.
Compute and interpret the range of a data set and state its limitation.
Define mean deviation about a central value using absolute deviations.
Calculate mean deviation about the mean and about the median for ungrouped data.

topics.title: Mean Deviation for Grouped Data and its Limitations

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate mean deviation about the mean or median for discrete and continuous frequency distributions.
State the limitations of mean deviation as a measure of dispersion.

topics.title: Variance and Standard Deviation of Ungrouped Data

concepts.learning_objective: Define variance and standard deviation and relate their units to the data.
Calculate variance and standard deviation of ungrouped data and use them to find unknown observations.
Calculate the variance and standard deviation of a discrete frequency distribution.
Calculate the standard deviation of a continuous frequency distribution using class mid-points.

topics.title: Shortcut Method and Effect of Changes on Variance

concepts.learning_objective: Use the step-deviation method to find mean, variance and standard deviation.
Determine how adding a constant to or multiplying the observations changes the mean, variance and standard deviation.
Recompute mean and standard deviation after correcting wrongly recorded observations.
Identify an event as a subset of the sample space of a random experiment.
Decide whether an event has occurred from the outcome of an experiment.
Recognise the impossible event and the sure event of an experiment.
Distinguish simple events from compound events.
Write the complement of an event as a subset of the sample space.
Express the events 'A or B' and 'A and B' as union and intersection of sets.
Express 'A but not B' and 'neither A nor B' using set operations.
Test whether two or more events are mutually exclusive.
Test whether a collection of events is exhaustive.

topics.title: Axiomatic approach and probability of an event

concepts.learning_objective: State the axioms of probability and their consequences such as P(empty set) = 0.
Find the probability of an event as the sum of the probabilities of its sample points.
Use equally likely outcomes to compute probabilities.

topics.title: Probability of 'A or B' and 'not A'

concepts.learning_objective: Apply P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).
Apply P(not A) = 1 - P(A).
